judged_text: The webhook decrypts keys and writes the parsed JSON straight into credential.key with no validation against the target app's credential schema and no backup of the previous key. A malformed or partial payload from the parent application (e.g. {} or keys missing refresh_token) silently replaces a working user credential; the old key is gone from the DB with no export or fallback, so the user's integration is destroyed and neither side sees an error — the handler still returns 200.

A malformed or partial payload from the parent application (e.g. {} or keys missing refresh_token) silently replaces a working user credential; the old key is gone from the DB with no export or fallback, so the user's integration is destroyed and neither side sees an error — the handler still returns 200.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts), the decrypted payload is `JSON.parse(...)`d and written directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: keys }})` / `create({ key: keys })` without validating `keys` against any app-specific credential schema (only `req.body` is zod-validated, and `keys` is just a string). This can overwrite an existing working credential with a malformed/partial object (e.g., missing refresh_token), and there is no backup/rollback of the previous `credential.key`. The handler returns 200 after update/create regardless of whether the stored key is usable by the integration later.
